newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps cuts Clorox note rating.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps cuts Clorox note rating.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Wednesday it has lowered its rating on Clorox Co's senior debt notes to Single-A-Plus from Double-A-Minus.
Duff & Phelps said Clorox's commercial paper rating was also downgraded, to D-One from D-One-Plus.
The action affects about $275 million of Clorox's debt, the firm said.
Duff & Phelps said the downgrades were made subject to the completion of Clorox's tender offer for Armor All Products Corp.

The offer of about $400 million for all of Armor's common stock is expected to begin on December 2 and to close before the end of the year. Financing for the acquisition will be provided by commercial paper, bank borrowings and excess free cash flow.

"Our rating action not only reflects the increased leverage from the current transaction, but also the expectation that Clorox will manage its capital structure more agressively going forward," Duff & Phelps said in a news release.
"Furthermore, our rating recognizes the company's strong free cash flow, which was in excess of $200 million for the 1996 fiscal yearend, and its significant financial flexibility," the firm said.
